name: ConfluxDB
tagline: Waterloo research prototype giving global snapshot isolation to partitioned, multi-master PostgreSQL.
description: ConfluxDB is a research prototype by Prima Chairunnanda, Khuzaima Daudjee and M. Tamer Özsu at the University of Waterloo, published in PVLDB in 2014. It targets a specific gap: providing snapshot isolation across a database that is partitioned over several primary sites that all accept updates, without restricting a transaction to one site or partitioning the workload in advance, while also letting read replicas see globally consistent snapshots. Distributed update transactions commit with two-phase commit while ConfluxDB determines a global order for them, and a log-merging replication scheme combines the primaries' update streams into a single stream consistent with that order, which every replica applies. The prototype was built on PostgreSQL; no public code release is known.
statusNote: Academic prototype described in PVLDB vol. 7 (2014); no public release.

scale.notes: Partitioned primaries plus replicas fed by a merged, SI-ordered update log.

strengths: Global snapshot isolation across several update-accepting partitions
Log-merging replication gives replicas SI-consistent snapshots without a single-master bottleneck
Builds on stock PostgreSQL concurrency control
weaknesses: Research prototype with no public code
Distributed updates still pay for two-phase commit
useCases: Studying replication protocols for snapshot isolation
Background for multi-master partitioned database research
